svg.title: macOS · Project import · already imported · 760×680
svg.desc: Mirrors App/ProjectImport.swift (ProjectImportSheet, phase .duplicate) over AppModel.importProject. Opening an archive the library already holds does NOT quietly make a second copy of a multi-gigabyte project — it asks. The match is on the id in the archive's manifest, tested against both the ids of projects here and the `importedFromID` recorded on projects imported earlier (AppModel.existingImport(of:)), so re-opening the same file finds the copy it made last time, and an archive exported from this Mac finds the project it came from. Import mints a fresh id for every project it creates — folder names key on it, so reusing the original would collide with the source device's own library — and `importedFromID` is the only thread back to where it came from; projects captured here, and projects imported before that field existed, have none. THE QUESTION IS ASKED AFTER UNPACKING, not before: the identifying id lives in project.json *inside* the archive, and reaching it early would mean decompressing the whole stream a second time on every import to spare the rare re-import. The staged tree waits on disk while the question is open — the import is suspended inside importProject on a continuation, not abandoned — and is deleted with the rest if the answer is no. NEITHER ANSWER IS A DEAD END and neither is destructive, which is why the default action (⏎) is the one that spends nothing: "Open the one I have" discards the staged tree and opens the existing project, leaving the library untouched; "Import again as a new project" installs a second, independent project alongside it, carrying the same `importedFromID`. Both land on a project detail. Sheet grows to 380×356 here, past the 300 floor, to seat the second button. Verified 2026-08-13 on the real 2.37 GB archive: second double-click raised this sheet with the library untouched at 24 projects; "Open the one I have" left it at 24 and cleared the staging tree; "Import again" made a 25th with a fresh id and the same origin.
